findings.title: any-typed context now yields union ctx after middleware
findings.why_it_matters: Apps whose context is typed `any` (`initTRPC.context<any>()`, or an untyped createContext) now get compile errors on arbitrary ctx properties in any procedure after a middleware that calls `next({ ctx })`. The cause is that `any extends object` resolves to BOTH branches. So `Overwrite<any, { user: number }>` becomes `{ user: number } | { [x: string]: any; ... }`, and `ctx.foo` fails with "Property 'foo' does not exist on type '{ user: number; }'". With the old `TType extends any` check, the any stayed on the true branch and produced an index-signature object, so `ctx.foo` compiled. Making the object test non-distributive for `any` restores the old behavior. It also keeps the per-member distribution that union contexts (issue-4321) rely on.
findings.suggested_fix: Distribute first with `extends any`, then test object-ness with a tuple-wrapped check so `any` resolves to a single branch: `type Overwrite<TType, TWith> = TType extends any ? [TType] extends [object] ? TWith extends any ? [TWith] extends [object] ? { [K in keyof TType | keyof TWith]: K extends keyof TWith ? TWith[K] : K extends keyof TType ? TType[K] : never } : TWith : never : TWith : never;` (verified in scratch: Fixed<any,{user:number}> allows `.foo` and `.user`, Fixed<string,string> = string, Fixed<{a:1}|{b:2},{c:3}> = {a:1;c:3}|{b:2;c:3}). Add a type test with `initTRPC.context<any>()` + `.use(o => o.next({ ctx: { user: 1 } }))` that accesses `ctx.foo`.
evidence: packages/server/src/core/internals/utils.ts:11 -- export type Overwrite<TType, TWith> = TType extends object

tsc scratch (new source): `initTRPC.context<any>().create(); t.procedure.use((o) => o.next({ ctx: { user: 1 } })).query(({ ctx }) => { ctx.foo; })` -> error TS2339: Property 'foo' does not exist on type '{ user: number; } | { [x: string]: any; [x: number]: any; [x: symbol]: any; } | ...'
tsc scratch (identical file against main's server source): no error
tsc scratch: `Overwrite<any, {}>` -> '{} | { [x: string]: any; ... }' (new) vs index-signature object (old)

findings.title: Array/Date inputs with middleware still infer mangled types
findings.why_it_matters: The PR's stated goal is correct inference for non-plain-object inputs followed by `.use(middleware)`. Array and Date inputs are still broken because arrays and Dates satisfy `extends object`, so they still go through the key-wise mapped type. `t.procedure.input(z.array(z.string())).use(o => o.next()).query(...)` still infers `inferRouterInputs[...]` as `{ [x: number]: string; [iterator]: ...; flat: ... }` instead of `string[]`. `z.date()` likewise yields a spread of Date's members. Client callers of such procedures keep getting unusable input and output types. The fix covers only primitives, and the new test only checks `z.string()`.
findings.suggested_fix: Only merge key-wise when both sides are plain object types: before the mapped branch, return TWith when either side is an array/tuple or a built-in class instance, e.g. `[TType] extends [readonly unknown[] | Date] ? TWith : [TWith] extends [readonly unknown[] | Date] ? TWith : <mapped merge>`. Assumption: runtime `createInputMiddleware` only spreads plain objects (`isPlainObject` rejects arrays), so for arrays the last parser's value wins and TWith is the matching type. Add `z.array(z.string())` and `z.date()` cases to issue-5020-inference-middleware.test.ts.
evidence: packages/server/src/core/middleware.ts:218-219 -- function isPlainObject(obj: unknown) { return obj && typeof obj === 'object' && !Array.isArray(obj); }

tsc scratch (new source): inferRouterInputs for `.input(z.array(z.string())).use((o) => o.next())` -> '{ [x: number]: string; [iterator]: () => IterableIterator<string>; ... flat: ... }' (same as main); `.input(z.date())` -> '{ [toPrimitive]: ...; toString: () => string; ... }'

findings.title: Doc says TType kept when TWith never; returns never
findings.why_it_matters: The new doc comment says TType is overwritten by TWith "unless TWith is never", which implies TType is kept when TWith is never. In fact `TWith extends any ? TWith : TType` distributes over `never` and returns `never`, so the `: TType` branch is unreachable. The object branch also returns never. Verified: `Overwrite<string, never>` and `Overwrite<{a:1}, never>` are both `never`. Runtime behavior is unchanged from before, but the comment and dead branch mislead anyone relying on the documented fallback.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the `: TType` fallback with `: never` and change the comment to say the result is `never` when TWith is `never`. Or, if keeping TType is intended, wrap it: `[TWith] extends [never] ? TType : TWith`.
evidence: tsc scratch: expectTypeOf<Overwrite<string, never>>().toEqualTypeOf<never>() and expectTypeOf<Overwrite<{ a: 1 }, never>>().toEqualTypeOf<never>() both pass

residual_risks: Overwrite<{ a: string }, unknown> changed from `{ a: string }` (old) to `unknown` (new). Input call sites are guarded by `UnsetMarker extends TNext['_input_in']` in procedureBuilder.ts:39/42. A `_ctx_out` of `unknown` (e.g. `next({ ctx: x as unknown })`) would now erase the whole context type. Not observed in repo usages (grep-only coverage).
testing_gaps: issue-5020-inference-middleware.test.ts defines `voidWithMiddleware` but never asserts its inferred input/output, so the stated goal of not regressing void inputs with middleware is untested.

No regression test covers object input + middleware + second object input merging, or a middleware-extended ctx over an `any`/union root context, which are the other Overwrite consumers this change touches (the existing tsc suite passes at head).
